text:
lina_support: Nimbus (nimbus_ops) opened a ticket — seeing p95 latency spikes and intermittent 429s from their eu2 dedicated pool starting ~09:20 UTC. They also report two 401s during autoscale. Suspect noisy neighbor on MIG slices. Anyone on call?

samir_infra: I'm on it. Can you paste the customer's pool id and a sample trace?

lina_support: Pool: eu2-ded-47, node: rdu-eu2-47, tenant: nimbus-prod. Attaching a short trace from their SDK: 
```
POST /v1/generate 200ms
-> token_forward 180ms
-> kv_cache_block 150ms
POST /v1/generate 429ms
-> auth 401 transient (token refresh)
```

maya_sre: nimbus-prod on a shared dedicated node with mixed MIG partitions? That smells like SM saturation on a sibling slice. I'll pull node telemetry (SM util, mem bw, GPU temp).

nico_eng: Quick check — did autoscale split or reassign slices at ~09:22? If we re-homed workloads it could cause transient auth races.

ops-bot: node-metrics rdu-eu2-47: {"timestamp":4082345660, "gpu0_sm":97, "gpu1_sm":6, "mem_bw_util":86, "sm_eff":0.98} 

maya_sre: gpu0 SM at 97%, sustained for ~2m during spike window. mem bw high. Looks like one MIG slice hogging SM. Also seeing frequent context-switches in kernel scheduler.

nico_eng: Hmm. KVCACHE locks reported in runtime logs around same time: "kv_cache_lock wait=120ms stack=..." That explains token forward latency. Could be contention on KV cache due to multiple tenants on same host.

lina_support: Customer says they run 3x bursty inference workers (concurrency ~12). They did a load test at 09:19 with short 15s bursts. Repro steps provided by customer: run 50 RPS for 30s to /v1/chat with seq len ~512.

samir_infra: Repro locally with a synthetic load on eu2-ded-47 (isolated window): small load triggers sibling SM saturation after ~10s when background tenant hits large batch. Will try to reproduce with MIG bookkeeping enabled.

nico_eng: Can you run this quick command on the node to see partition layout + process assignment: 
```
sudo nvidia-smi mig -lgi && ps -ef | grep redwood-runtime
```

ops-bot: mig-layout rdu-eu2-47: GPU0: MIGs [7g.40gb, 2g.20gb], GPU1: MIGs [3g.20gb, 1g.10gb] 

maya_sre: That 7g slice is likely hosting the noisy tenant. Plan: 1) Offload noisy slice to a spare node (live migrate by draining requests), 2) Short-term: bump autoscale cooldown to avoid token refresh races, 3) Investigate runtime K/V cache locking and consider per-tenant cache shards.

nico_eng: For immediate mitigation, I can push a sticky-routing override to prevent nimbus-prod from landing on the same physical GPU as the noisy tenant. Also propose enabling fractional isolation for their pool (reserved slice) if they want guaranteed isolation.

lina_support: Nimbus asked about billing — they saw a cost spike due to retries during the 429 window. billing-bot, any idea how to surface to them?

billing-bot: Created billing note linked to ticket #INC-3821. We can show token usage delta and mark spike window 09:18-09:25 UTC. Offer to credit incremental cost from retries after engineering confirms root cause.

maya_sre: Also noticed two auth 401s in trace — likely due to ephemeral token refresh triggered by client retry loop during autoscale. Suggest increasing token validity on autoscale events or delaying in-flight token rotation until draining completes.

samir_infra: I drained the noisy slice and rebalanced at 09:28. Post-drain metrics show gpu0_sm dropped to 12% and p95 for nimbus-prod returned to baseline ~120ms. KVCACHE contention gone.

nico_eng: Follow-ups: 1) runtime change — add per-tenant shard for KV cache (low-risk config), 2) infra policy — add autoscale-stabilization hold to avoid token rotations during live rehoming, 3) offering to move nimbus-prod to reserved slice for predictable latency.

lina_support: Nimbus is asking for short repro instructions so they can validate before we close. Please add a short checklist I can send.

maya_sre: Send them: 1) Run the provided 50 RPS/30s load to reproduce. 2) On our side check `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` and runtime logs for "kv_cache_lock". 3) If you see sustained gpu SM >=90% on one slice and KV lock >50ms, open support. 4) As a workaround set client retry backoff and contact us to schedule a reserved slice move.

nico_eng: I'll open an RFC for per-tenant KV shards and flag as P1 for this week.

lina_support: Thanks — I'll update the ticket and propose a credit for retry-cost once infra confirms the noisy neighbor timeline. :thumbsup:

nimbus_ops: Thanks team — we'll run the checklist and ping when we have the traces. Appreciate the fast response.

ops-bot: ticket INC-3821 updated: mitigation applied, status -> investigating, assignees -> samir_infra, nico_eng

lina_support: Closing loop here — putting follow-up action items in the ticket and scheduling a short postmortem if RFC changes go in.
